chen2018-pov-circuit-setup: Section 2, p.5: the paper states its circuit is a general POVM with 4 outcomes and uses 2 ancilla qubits. Read in context with Eq. 2.4-2.5.
chen2018-cost-function-definition: Section 2, Eq. 2.6, p.6: the paper defines J1 with the success term, the alpha-err penalty and the alpha-inc penalty, and explains the three parts in the next sentences.
chen2018-adam-settings: Section 3, footnote 3, p.7: 50 sub-samples, beta1, beta2, epsilon-hat and rate 0.001 as quoted; Section 2, p.6: forward differences. The footnote also gives the step size 1e-6, which the value omits; nothing in the value is overstated.
chen2018-train-test-set-sizes: Section 3, footnotes 4 and 5, p.7: 100 evenly spaced training points, 150 i.i.d. test points, 5000 Adam iterations, as quoted.
chen2018-centred-data-sampling: Section 3, footnote 1, p.6 and p.7: 100 i.i.d. points, normal with mean a0 and variance 0.01, truncated to [0,1]; test set {a0}. Note the Fig. 2 and Fig. 3 captions call 0.01 the standard deviation; the value follows the footnote wording.
chen2018-larger-qubits-open: Appendix C, p.16: the authors state they saw stable optimisation only up to the qubit numbers used and leave open whether it holds for larger numbers. It is their own stated limit.
chen2018-preprint-status: Section 1 footer, p.1: the page-1 footer reads 'Preprint. Work in progress.' The paper states its own status.
chen2018-simulated-exact-probabilities: Section 5, p.13 (and Section 3, p.6: 'numerical experiments performed on classical hardware using the exact probabilities'): the paper states its experiments ran on a simulated quantum computer with exact measurement probabilities.
qlstm-training-setup: Section V, p.13: N = 4, rescale to [-1,1], 67%/33% split, max 100 epochs, RMSprop with eta 0.01, alpha 0.99, eps 1e-8 for both models, PennyLane and Qulacs. All stated in the passage.
qlstm-test-systems-setup: Section V.B, p.15-19: pendulum parameters and initial angular velocity 3 rad/s (p.15), J2 (p.16), delayed quantum feedback system (p.17-18), population inversion with g = 1, n-bar 40, nmax 100 (p.19). The value names the waveguide system without parameters and the paper gives none beyond sinusoidal modulation.
qlstm-architecture-definition: Section IV, p.7-12, Fig. 4-5, Eq. (5): the paper defines the QLSTM cell with six VQCs, VQC1-4 on the concatenated vector with sigmoid or tanh, VQC5 to the hidden state, VQC6 to the output, and each block with three layers.
qlstm-encoding-variational-layer: Section IV.A p.8-9 and IV.B p.10: H, Ry(arctan x), Rz(arctan x^2), arctan chosen over arcsin and arccos, CNOTs with fixed adjacency 1 and 2 cyclic, then rotations, depth 2, Pauli Z expectation of each qubit. All defined by the paper.
qlstm-large-scale-impractical: Section VI, p.21: the authors say large-scale time-dependent modelling is impractical due to simulator and ML framework performance, and leave noise robustness to future work.
qlstm-noiseless-no-nisq-training: Section VI, p.21 (PDF page 21; the stored anchor says page 20): the authors state they assumed a perfect quantum computer and that NISQ training remains a significant challenge due to circuit evaluations.
qlstm-setup-param-counts: Section V, p.12-13: hidden size 5, 166 classical parameters, 6 VQCs with 4 qubits and depth 2, 2 scaling parameters, 6 x 4 x 2 x 3 + 2 = 146, all stated. The widened value is exactly the passage.
chen2022-hyperparameters: Section 6.2, p.4: batch size 8, Adam 1e-3, buffer 100, lookup steps 10, S = 4 soft update with tau 1e-2, as quoted.
chen2022-epsilon-schedule: Section 6.2, p.4: epsilon multiplied by 0.995 from 0.1 to a final 0.001, as quoted.
chen2022-cartpole-environment: Section 6.1, p.3-4: four-dimensional observation, actions +1 and -1, reward +1 per upright step, termination at 15 degrees or 2.4 units. Matches the paper.
chen2022-qlstm-model-definition: Section 5.1-5.2, p.3: the paper gives the QLSTM cell equations (2a-2f), Fig. 4 circuit, the encoding and variational parts, and defines the dressed QLSTM. QLSTM first came from reference [38], but the paper restates and uses the definition fully.
chen2022-wells-fargo-disclaimer: Section 1 footnote, p.1: the paper states its views are the authors' and not Wells Fargo's, and that it is not investment advice. The paper's own statement about its scope.
chen2022-qdrqn-setup: Section 6.1 p.3 and 6.3 p.4: 8-qubit VQCs, input and hidden dimension 4, 1 or 2 VQC layers, Cart-Pole. All stated.
rc-qrnn-rc-configuration: Section V.B, p.13 and Section III, p.6: RC runs freeze all quantum parameters after random initialization, train classical parameters only, and use the same hyperparameters as full optimization; no quantum gradients are needed.
rc-quantum-model-sizes: Section V.A p.13 and Section IV p.7-10: 24, 72, 144 quantum parameters and 4, 4, 5 classical parameters; 48, 144, 288 for NARMA; input 1-d, hidden 3-d, QLSTM cell state 4-d, last step t = 4. All stated.
rc-classical-baseline-sizes: Section V.D, p.14: RNN 40, GRU 120, LSTM 160 parameters, each with 6 in the final linear layer; recurrent parameters frozen for RC. Stated as quoted.
rc-training-scheme: Section V p.12 and Section VI p.16: N = 4, 67%/33% split, RMSprop with 0.01, 0.99, 1e-8 (Section V.A p.13), PyTorch, PennyLane, Qiskit for noisy simulation.
rc-noise-model: Section V.C, p.13-14: serial thermal relaxation and depolarization, IBM Peekskill upper-limit parameters, T1 N(500,50) us, T2 N(400,40) us, gate times 0, 20, 300, 700, 800 ns, depolarization N(1e-4,1e-5) and N(1e-3,1e-4). Matches the value.
rc-task-definitions: Section V.E, p.14-15: damped pendulum parameters and 3 rad/s initial velocity, J2, NARMA coefficients, input constants (2.11, 3.73, 4.11, 100), M = 300, n0 = 5 and 10. Matches the value.
rc-wells-fargo-disclaimer: Acknowledgments, p.30: the paper states the views are the authors' and not Wells Fargo's, and that it is not investment advice.
qrnn-rc-setup: Abstract p.1 and Section V.B p.13: the paper states that the QRNN with random weights is treated as a dynamical system and only the final classical linear layer is trained. The abstract sentence is verbatim; Section V.B confirms the frozen quantum parameters.
chen2023-hyperparameters: Section VI.B, p.11: Adam 1e-4, beta1 0.92, beta2 0.999, S = 5, gamma 0.9, as quoted.
chen2023-environments: Section VI.A, p.9-11: Acrobot reward threshold -100, Cart-Pole 15 degrees and 2.4 units, MiniGrid-SimpleCrossing 7x7x3 = 147 observation, six actions, n = 9, sparse reward. Matches the value.
chen2023-evaluation-metric: Section VI.B, p.13: the paper states results are scores from the past 100 episodes averaged.
chen2023-vqc-architecture: Sections IV-V, Fig. 1 and 3, p.6-9 and Section VI.B p.11: the paper defines the dressed VQC, linear layers before and after (input to qubits, output to actions or 1), Pauli-Z expectation values from shots, and separate actor and critic VQCs.
chen2023-qa3c-framework: Section V, p.7-9 and Algorithm 1: the paper defines the global shared memory, local copies, upload and download of gradients and the update every S steps or at terminal state.
chen2023-software-simulation: Section VI.B, p.12: PennyLane for circuits and PyTorch overall. The clause 'no noise model and no quantum hardware run' is not quoted; it is an absence, but a search of the full text finds no noise model or hardware run and the paper says 'numerical simulations' (abstract, conclusion). Grade high on the stated software; the absence clause is read from the whole text.
chen2023-wells-fargo-disclaimer: Acknowledgments, p.15: the paper states the views are the authors' and not Wells Fargo's, and that it is not investment advice.
chen2023-setup-simulation-8-qubits: Section VI.B, p.11-13: 8 qubits, two variational layers, 8 x 3 x 2 = 48 per VQC and 96 in total, 80 CPU cores and parallel agents; abstract and conclusion say numerical simulations. All stated.

theory_low.chen2018-measurement-repetitions-ideal: Section 4, p.9 and footnote 6: an order-of-magnitude estimate (1/eps^4, 1e12 for eps = 1e-3) resting on an assumed normal cost distribution with an assumed variance. It is an informal argument, not a proved result.
theory_low.qlstm-circuit-evaluation-scaling: Section VI, p.21: the O(nms) growth is a one-sentence counting argument, not a proof, and the inference scaling O(ms') is a hedged possibility ('it could be possible'). The cost limit itself is already carried by the NISQ-training item. m = 6, n = 146, s = 200 to 2000 are setup facts but the value centres on the scaling.
